tasks.redPrompt:
RED for #255 (rules: _shared of teams/mvox-dev/memory/pipeline-args/args-255.json — read it first; the issue thread IS the contract, read all comments). Six pinned areas.

(A) DEACTIVATE WRITE + REFUSAL. Admin-only deactivate from the roster: member.status moves off 'active', NOTHING else on the entity changes (done-when 1 — pin no other property writes, no _parent change, no rights change). Wire per house precedent for property replace (clear-then-set order, see updateRsvpStatus tests in rsvpData.spec.ts — POST appends on Entu, so replace = clear existing value then set). Two-step confirm matching the page's existing destructive idiom (pin reuse, not a new shape). REFUSAL while the person holds a manageable role grant (_owner/_editor via the fetchRights/roleManagement reads): deactivate is REFUSED with copy that NAMES THE REMEDY — who holds what role and where to remove it ('still an administrator of {collective}; remove the role on the admin page first') — never a bare 'cannot deactivate' (Gama binding; the #252 failure in message form). GREEN states whether the control is ALSO pre-disabled at render — RED asserts the refusal path regardless. Done-when 7: collective admin only; a member cannot deactivate herself or anyone.

(B) INACTIVE SURFACE + REINSTATE (done-when 4). Somewhere OUT of the main roster's normal flow to see inactive members and reinstate WITHOUT a fresh invitation (status back to 'active'). BINDING (adopted by Gama): the surface SHOWS each inactive member's section assignment — this is what explains the section ghost-blocker (deleteSection's deliberately unscoped count) with zero write-path change. Pin: _parent NOT cleared on deactivate; section shown on the surface.

(C) HISTORY UNION IN-SLICE (done-when 3 + acceptance §2). Season summary (attendanceSummary.ts + its call site): a deactivated member's rows STAY, marked inactive, showing attended COUNT and NO RATE. Pin absence of any percentage/denominator for inactive rows. The no-rate reasoning must live in a CODE COMMENT AT THE SITE (Gama binding — 'total counts events occurring after she was gone, so any percentage is wrong in a way that reads as a judgement about the person; no honest denominator exists without a deactivation date, which done-when 1 forbids') — RED may pin the comment's presence via a marker assertion or leave to review; state which.

(D) GOING-TALLY FOLD-IN (Gama's pre-build question, answered by Finn, folds under done-when 2; REFINED by Gama 15:31 — the join is DATE-GATED). loadTally at event/[id]/+page.svelte:398-419 computes going as a raw filter over ALL rsvp rows — not roster-joined, no date gate — and feeds the capacity line ('{going} / {capacity} kohta'). Pin BOTH directions: (i) FUTURE event — counts join against the ACTIVE roster (attendanceSummary precedent): a deactivated member's 'going' no longer inflates a count the conductor plans around; (ii) PAST event — tally stays AS RECORDED, raw and unjoined: she said yes, she very likely sang, the record says so; dropping her would rewrite a historical number on the basis of present membership (the same wrong as showing a rate). Use the page's EXISTING pastness logic for the gate — do not invent a new date comparison — and gate on THE EVENT THE TALLY WAS REQUESTED FOR, not the live $derived: isPast (:669) is derived off the CURRENTLY LOADED event while loadTally runs in async paths behind a generation guard (:300/:430/:569), so reading isPast inside a .then() reads pastness at resolution time — the stale-closure trap; the correct per-event form already exists in the file (isPastDetail(d), :673, used at :757) or capture the value at call time. RED should pin this with a test where the gate value is captured for the requested event (Bentham pre-branch finding). BOUNDARY, stated deliberately: pastness is event START (startAt < now, :669) — an event in progress counts as past and keeps the raw tally; if the build picks a different boundary it must be a STATED deviation, not an accident. Her rsvp ROW is never deleted either way. Two-hop server-side join impossible (Entu single-hop) — join is client-side; mock roster + rsvp rows with a deactivated member present, assert excluded-when-future AND counted-when-past. ESCAPE HATCH (Gama): if the date gate costs more than a conditional (timezone boundary, cache not knowing the date), ship the future-event fix alone and SAY SO in the report — the past case gets filed separately, do not widen the slice.

(E) SIGN-IN NOTICE (done-when 6 + acceptance §4). Membership resolution lifted into a store on the completionGate precedent; a STATUS-UNSCOPED self-lookup distinguishes 'deactivated' from 'never a member'. One app-level notice for the deactivated state; existing zero-code non-member degrade (rsvp_non_member_hint) stays for both. TRI-STATE FAIL-SAFE VERBATIM: a FAILED lookup must NEVER show the notice (pin it — a failed lookup telling an active member she has been removed is the worst available outcome). NO redirect, NO nav lock (both refusals accepted — pin their absence). COPY BINDING: 'not active' — never 'removed'/'deleted'/'deactivated' in user-facing strings; points at the choir, not support. Adjacent fact to leave alone: her own prior RSVP on a future event stays visible to her, disabled via the existing non-member path — pin unchanged.

(F) GHOST-FREE VERIFY (done-when 2). The active-scoped reads (listActiveMembers rosterData.ts:100, findMyMemberId rsvpData.ts:45) drop her for free — pin one roster test + one rsvp-eligibility test with a non-active member. Attendance panels are naturally safe (roster-driven iteration) — pin one comparison-panel test that a deactivated member's rsvp map entry renders no row.

New i18n keys (done-when 8): all new copy in 4 locales — GREEN translates; RED asserts via key mocks. Full-shape assertions throughout (toEqual over objectContaining). Do NOT touch: performReparent/roster arrange code (#253 just landed), AgendaList (#250 may be mid-flight — branch from main AFTER #250's merge; the pipeline checks out fresh main).

(2) Refusal-while-granted: read grants via existing fetchRights/roleManagement path; refusal copy names role + place (admin page); STATE in your report whether you also pre-disable at render and why (Gama requires the statement, either choice is acceptable). tasks.commitBody:
A member can now be deactivated: the member entity's status moves
off 'active' and nothing else about her changes — no deletion, no
rights change, no section change. Reversible from a new inactive-
members surface (outside the roster's normal flow) that shows each
inactive member's section assignment — which is also what explains
a section that refuses deletion while holding only inactive
members — and reinstates without a fresh invitation.

Deactivation REFUSES while the person still holds an admin or
librarian grant, naming the role and where to remove it. Refusing
beats auto-stripping for three independent reasons (PO ruling on
the engineering proposal): every person is _editor on her own
person entity, so a person-scoped strip would destroy her own
profile editing; there is no transaction to make strip-then-flip
atomic; and an action named 'deactivate' must not silently change
who administers the collective.

History keeps its subject — the reason deactivate beat delete. The
season summary keeps her rows, marked inactive, showing attended
counts without a rate: there is no honest denominator without a
deactivation date, and adding one is ruled out. The reasoning
lives in a comment at the site. The event-detail going-tally now
joins against the active roster, so a deactivated member's old
'yes' no longer inflates a count a conductor plans around; her
answer itself is kept.

On sign-in she is told the truth in neutral words — her membership
is not active, ask the choir — via a status-unscoped self-lookup
that can tell 'was a member' from 'never was'. A failed lookup
never shows the notice; no redirect; no navigation lock. She keeps
what she legitimately holds: domain-wide reads and her own
history.

Live gate (Mihkel): deactivate a test member in mvox_crede —
roster drops her, summary keeps her count without a rate, her
future-event 'going' leaves the tally, her sign-in shows the
notice; reinstate brings her back whole.
